BiblicalUsage: Yâqôwsh is the snarer himself, the fowler whose trap waits in every path. Hosea says the prophet has become a snare of a fowler in all his ways, with hatred in the house of his God.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a watchman turned snarer is the saddest sight in Scripture, and God will call him to account.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
